metadata.title: Computable upper error bounds for Krylov approximations to matrix exponentials and associated phi-functions

extraction_notes.note: definition or assumption: 'We assume ... we will refer to this assumption as the nonexpansive case' both imposes an assumption and names it; typed definition because later results use the term.
remark or algorithm: these remark environments propose an estimator and a step size iteration; kept as remarks since they are presented as suggestions, not as stated procedures.

The restarted-Krylov procedure and the Err_a step size rule are described in running text interleaved with notation; the algorithm spans include the interleaved definitions and the steps cover only the operations.

Figures, tables of step sizes and the descriptive list of compared codes (Expokit, tr.quad, eff.o.quad, a priori estimates) in Section 8, the longer quadrature expansions with D_m^[3], and the introduction's literature survey were not made nodes.
The Hermitian effective-order display writes $({\rm e}^{{\rm i}\,t\,T_m}e_1)_m$ where $({\rm e}^{t\,T_m}e_1)_m$ is meant; copied verbatim.

nodes.name: Matrix exponential applied to a vector, $E(t)v = e^{\sigma tA}v$
nodes.statement: E(t)v = {\rm e}^{\sigma\,t A} v, \quad A \in \mathbb C^{n\times n},~~\sigma\in\mathbb C,
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: exp(itA)v

nodes.name: Krylov identity (Arnoldi decomposition)
nodes.statement: A\,V_m = V_m T_m + \tau_{m+1,m}\,v_{m+1}e_m^\ast
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: krylovidentity

nodes.name: Vanishing entries $e_m^\ast T_m^j e_1 = 0$
nodes.statement: e_m^\ast\,T_m^{j}\,e_1 = 0 \quad \text{for}~~ j=0,\ldots,m-2,
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: eTe

nodes.name: Krylov reproduction of powers $A^j v = V_m T_m^j e_1$
nodes.statement: A^{j}v = V_m T_m^{j} e_1,~~~0\leq j \leq m-1,
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: HVTm

nodes.name: Definition of $\gamma_m$
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: gammam

nodes.name: Standard Krylov approximation $S_m(t)v$
nodes.statement: S_m(t)v = V_m\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,t T_m}\,V_m^\ast\,v = V_m\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,t T_m}e_1.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: Smv

nodes.name: Krylov error operator $L_m(t)$
nodes.statement: L_m(t)=E(t)-S_m(t) \in \mathbb C^{n \times n}.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: Lerror

nodes.name: Defect-based integral representation of the error
nodes.statement: L_m(t)v = \int_0^t E(t-s)\,D_m(s)v\,\mathrm{d} s.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: LDint

nodes.name: Explicit representation of the defect $D_m(s)v$
nodes.statement: D_m(s)v &= \sigma\,A\,V_m\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,s\,T_m}e_1 - \sigma\,V_m T_m\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,s\,T_m}e_1 = \sigma\,(A\,V_m - V_m T_m)\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,s\,T_m}e_1 \notag \\ &= \sigma \tau_{m+1,m}\,\big(e_m^\ast\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,s\,T_m}e_1\big)\,v_{m+1}.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: Dm(s)v

nodes.name: Leading term of the defect
nodes.statement: D_m(t)v = \sigma \tau_{m+1,m}\,\gamma_m\frac{(\sigma t)^{m-1}}{(m-1)!}\,v_{m+1} + {\mathcal{O}}(t^m),
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: Dm-lead

nodes.name: Orders of defect and error
nodes.statement: \| D_m(t)v \| = {\mathcal{O}}(t^{m-1}), \quad \text{and} \quad \| L_m(t)v \| = {\mathcal{O}}(t^{m}).
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: orderofDmLm

nodes.name: Leading term of the Krylov error
nodes.statement: L_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m\,\frac{(\sigma\,t)^{m}}{m!}v_{m+1} + R_{m+1}(t), \quad R_{m+1}(t) = {\mathcal{O}}(t^{m+1}),
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: asy-leading

nodes.name: Taylor expansion of the error
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &L_m(t)v = E(t)v - S_m(t)v = \frac{(\sigma\,t)^m}{{m!}}(A^m v - V_m T_m^m\,e_1) + R_{m+1}(t),\\ &\text{with Taylor remainder}~~ R_{m+1}(t) = {\mathcal{O}}(t^{m+1}). \end{aligned}
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.label: prop-3-proof

nodes.name: Definition of $\delta_m(s)$
nodes.statement: \delta_m(s) = e_m^\ast\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,s\,T_m}e_1 = \big( {\rm e}^{\sigma\,s\,T_m} \big)_{m,1},
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.label: defdelta

nodes.name: Defect-integral upper bound on the error
nodes.statement: \|L_m(t)v\|_2 \leq \tau_{m+1,m} \int_0^t |\delta_m(s)| \, \mathrm{d} s.
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.label: errorapprox1

nodes.name: Exponential of $T_m$ as Hermite interpolant
nodes.statement: {\rm e}^{\sigma\,t T_m} = p_t(T_m),
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.label: pt

nodes.name: Scalar exponential $f_t(\lambda)$
nodes.statement: {f_t}(\lambda) = {\rm e}^{\sigma\,t\lambda}
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.label: def:thetadd

nodes.name: Spectrum and field of values inclusion
nodes.statement: \text{spec}(\sigma\,T_m) \subseteq W(\sigma\,T_m) \subseteq W(\sigma\,A) \subseteq \mathbb C_-.
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.label: subsetofspectrum

nodes.name: Divided-difference representation of $\delta_m$
nodes.statement: \delta_m(t) = \divdif{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m}{f_t} \gamma_m \leq {\frac{t^{m-1}}{(m-1)!}\,\gamma_m,}
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.label: deltam-repr

nodes.name: Upper error bound $\mathrm{Err}_a$
nodes.statement: \| L_m(t)v \|_2 \leq \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m\,\frac{t^{m}}{m!}
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.label: asyerrest

nodes.name: Error estimate $\mathrm{Err}_a$
nodes.statement: \tag{$\mathrm{Err}_a$} \mathrm{Err}_a = \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m\,\frac{t^{m}}{m!}.
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.label: errornew

nodes.name: Asymptotic correctness of $\mathrm{Err}_a$
nodes.statement: \| L_m(t)v \|_2 = \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m\,\frac{t^m}{m!} + {\mathcal{O}}(t^{m+1}).
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}

nodes.name: Power series of $\varphi_p$
nodes.statement: \varphi_p(z) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{z^k}{(k+p)!}, \quad p\geq 0.
nodes.section: 4 Krylov approximation to $\varphi$-functions.
nodes.label: defphiseries

nodes.name: Integral representation of $\varphi_p$
nodes.statement: \varphi_p(z) = \frac{1}{(p-1)!} \int_0^1 (1-\theta)^{p-1}{\rm e}^{\theta z}\,\mathrm{d}\theta, \quad p \geq 1.
nodes.section: 4 Krylov approximation to $\varphi$-functions.
nodes.label: defphiint

nodes.name: Krylov approximation of $\varphi_p$
nodes.statement: \varphi_p(\sigma\,t A)v \approx V_m \varphi_p(\sigma\,t T_m) e_1,~~~~p\geq 0.
nodes.section: 4 Krylov approximation to $\varphi$-functions.
nodes.label: kry-phi

nodes.name: Error $L^p_m(t)v$ of the $\varphi$-function approximation
nodes.statement: L^p_m(t)v = \varphi_p(\sigma\,t\,A)v - V_m \varphi_p(\sigma\,t\,T_m) e_1.
nodes.section: 4 Krylov approximation to $\varphi$-functions.
nodes.label: generalizeerrornotation

nodes.name: Leading term of $L^p_m(t)v$
nodes.statement: L^p_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m}\,\gamma_m \frac{(\sigma\, t)^m}{(m+p)!} \, v_{m+1} + \mathcal{O}(t^{m+1}).
nodes.section: 4 Krylov approximation to $\varphi$-functions.
nodes.label: leadingtermphij

nodes.name: Upper bound on $\|L^p_m(t)v\|_2$
nodes.statement: \|L^p_m(t)v \|_2 \leq \tau_{m+1,m}\,\gamma_m\,\frac{t^{m}}{(m+p)!},
nodes.section: 4 Krylov approximation to $\varphi$-functions.
nodes.label: eresphij

nodes.statement: L_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m}\,\sigma\,t \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} e_m^\ast\varphi_{j}(\sigma\,tT_m)\,e_1 (\sigma\,t A)^{j-1}v_{m+1}.

nodes.statement: \tag{$\mathrm{Err}_1$} \mathrm{Err}_1 = \tau_{m+1,m}\,t\,|e_m^\ast\varphi_1(\sigma\,t T_m)e_1|.

nodes.statement: {T}^+_m = \begin{bmatrix} T_m&0\\ \tau_{m+1,m}\,e_m^\ast&0 \end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb C^{(m+1)\times (m+1)}

nodes.name: nonexpansive case
nodes.statement: We assume that $\mu_2(\sigma A)\leq 0$, where $\mu_2(\sigma A)$ denotes the logarithmic norm of $\sigma A$, or equivalently, $W(\sigma A)\subseteq \mathbb C_-$, where $W(\sigma A)$ denotes the field of values of $\sigma A$ and we will refer to this assumption as the \emph{nonexpansive case}.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.statement_short: Assumption that the logarithmic norm of $\sigma A$ is nonpositive (field of values in the closed left half-plane).

nodes.name: Nonexpansive evolution bound
nodes.statement: $\mu_2(\sigma A)\leq 0$ implies $\|E(t)\|_2\leq 1$ for $t\geq 0$.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error

nodes.name: Krylov subspace
nodes.statement: The numerical approximation of~\eqref{exp(itA)v} considered here (see~\eqref{Smv} below) is based on the conventional Krylov subspace \begin{equation*} \mathcal{K}_m(A,v) = \mathrm{span}\{v,A v,\ldots,A^{m-1}v\} \subseteq \mathbb C^n. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error

nodes.name: Arnoldi iteration and Krylov identity
nodes.statement: First, \tjnew{an orthonormal} basis of $ \mathcal{K}_m(A,v) $ is obtained by the well-known Arnoldi iteration, see~\cite{saad03}. This produces a basis matrix $ V_m \in \mathbb C^{n \times m} $ satisfying $ V_m^\ast\,V_m = I_{m \times m} $, and an upper Hessenberg matrix $ T_m \in \mathbb C^{m\times m} $ such that the Krylov identity\footnote{ Here, $ {e_m = (0,\ldots,0,1)^\ast \in \mathbb C^m} $, and in the sequel we also denote $ {e_1 = (1,0,\ldots,0)^\ast \in \mathbb C^m} $.} \begin{equation} A\,V_m = V_m T_m + \tau_{m+1,m}\,v_{m+1}e_m^\ast \end{equation} is valid, with $\tau_{m+1,m}\in\mathbb R_+$ and $v_{m+1}\in\mathbb C^n$ with $\|v_{m+1}\|_2=1$.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.statement_short: Arnoldi yields orthonormal $V_m$, upper Hessenberg $T_m$, $\tau_{m+1,m}>0$ and $v_{m+1}$ with $AV_m = V_mT_m + \tau_{m+1,m}v_{m+1}e_m^\ast$.

nodes.name: Lucky breakdown of the Arnoldi iteration
nodes.statement: We are assuming that the Arnoldi iteration is executed until the desired dimension~$ m $. Then, by construction, all lower diagonal entries of $ T_m $ are positive~\cite{saad03}. If this is not the case, i.e., if a breakdown occurs, it is known that this breakdown is {\em lucky,}, i.e., the approximation~\eqref{Smv} below obtained in the step before breakdown is already exact, see~\cite{saad92s}.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error

nodes.name: Lanczos iteration for Hermitian $A$
nodes.statement: For the case of a Hermitian matrix $A$ the Krylov subspace can be constructed using the Lanczos iteration, which is a special case of the Arnoldi iteration, resulting in a tridiagonal matrix $ T_m \in \mathbb R^{m \times m} $. In the following we discuss the general case and comment on the case of \tjnew{a Hermitian} matrix~$ A $ whenever appropriate.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error

nodes.name: Krylov polynomial identities
nodes.statement: The following identities hold true due to the upper Hessenberg [tridiagonal] structure of~$ T_m $ together with~\eqref{krylovidentity}: \begin{equation} e_m^\ast\,T_m^{j}\,e_1 = 0 \quad \text{for}~~ j=0,\ldots,m-2, \end{equation} and \tjnew{ \begin{equation} A^{j}v = V_m T_m^{j} e_1,~~~0\leq j \leq m-1, \end{equation} see for instance~\cite[Theorem 2]{DK89} or~\cite{saad92s}.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
assumptions: the upper Hessenberg [tridiagonal] structure of~$ T_m $ together with~\eqref{krylovidentity}
conclusions: A^{j}v = V_m T_m^{j} e_1,~~~0\leq j \leq m-1,
nodes.statement_short: $e_m^\ast T_m^j e_1=0$ for $j\le m-2$ and $A^jv=V_mT_m^je_1$ for $j\le m-1$.

nodes.name: $\gamma_m$ (product of subdiagonal entries)
nodes.statement: Furthermore, let \begin{equation} \gamma_m = e_m^\ast\,T_m^{m-1} e_1 = \prod_{j=1}^{m-1} (T_m)_{j+1,j}\,, \end{equation} where the claimed identity also follows from the upper Hessenberg [tridiagonal] structure of~$ T_m $.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error

nodes.name: Standard Krylov approximation
nodes.statement: The standard Krylov approximation to $ E(t)v $ is \begin{equation} S_m(t)v = V_m\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,t T_m}\,V_m^\ast\,v = V_m\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,t T_m}e_1. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error

nodes.name: Krylov error operator
nodes.statement: We denote the corresponding error operator by $ L_m(t) $, with \begin{equation} L_m(t)=E(t)-S_m(t) \in \mathbb C^{n \times n}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error

nodes.name: defect operator
nodes.statement: We define the \emph{defect}\, operator $ D_m(t) $ of $ S_m(t) $ by \begin{equation*} D_m(t) = \sigma\,A\,S_m(t) - S_m'(t) \in \mathbb C^{n \times n}. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error

nodes.name: Defect-based integral representation of the error
nodes.statement: Then, $ L_m(t)v $ and $ D_m(t)v $ are related via the differential equation \begin{equation*} L_m'(t)v = \sigma\,A\,L_m(t)v + D_m(t)v, \quad L_m(0)v=0, \end{equation*} whence \begin{equation} L_m(t)v = \int_0^t E(t-s)\,D_m(s)v\,\mathrm{d} s. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.statement_short: Variation-of-constants: the error is the integral of the propagated defect.

nodes.name: Leading term of the Krylov error
nodes.statement: \noindent For any $ A \in \mathbb C^{\tjnew{n \times n}} $ the error $ L_m(t)v $ satisfies the asymptotic relation \begin{equation} L_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m\,\frac{(\sigma\,t)^{m}}{m!}v_{m+1} + R_{m+1}(t), \quad R_{m+1}(t) = {\mathcal{O}}(t^{m+1}), \end{equation} for $ t \to 0 $.
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
conclusions: the error $ L_m(t)v $ satisfies the asymptotic relation
nodes.statement_short: $L_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m(\sigma t)^m/m!\,v_{m+1}+O(t^{m+1})$ as $t\to0$.
nodes.label: prop:prop3

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (leading error term)
nodes.statement: Taylor expansion. Due to $ L_m(t)v = {\mathcal{O}}(t^m) $, \tjnew{see~\eqref{orderofDmLm},} \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &L_m(t)v = E(t)v - S_m(t)v = \frac{(\sigma\,t)^m}{{m!}}(A^m v - V_m T_m^m\,e_1) + R_{m+1}(t),\\ &\text{with Taylor remainder}~~ R_{m+1}(t) = {\mathcal{O}}(t^{m+1}). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Multiplying the identity~\tjnew{{\eqref{HVTm}} (with $ j = m-1 $) by $ A $} and using~\eqref{krylovidentity} gives \begin{align*} A^m\,v &= A\,V_m T_m^{m-1} e_1 = (V_m T_m + \tau_{m+1,m}\,v_{m+1} e_m^\ast) T_m^{m-1} e_1 \\ &= V_m T_m^m\,e_1 + \tau_{m+1,m}\, (e_m^\ast\,T_m^{m-1} e_1)\,v_{m+1} = V_m T_m^m\,e_1 + \tau_{m+1,m} \gamma_m v_{m+1}, \end{align*} whence~\eqref{prop-3-proof} simplifies to~\eqref{asy-leading}. \qed
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.statement_short: Taylor expansion, then multiply the Krylov power identity by $A$ and use the Krylov identity.

nodes.name: Explicit Taylor remainder
nodes.statement: The Taylor remainder $ R_{m+1} $ in~\eqref{asy-leading} can be specified in a more explicit way showing its dependence on~$ m $, $$ R_{m+1}(t) = \frac{(\sigma\,t)^{m+1}}{m!} \int_{0}^{1} \big(A^{m+1} {\rm e}^{\sigma\,\theta\,t\,A} v - V_m T_m^{m+1}{\rm e}^{\sigma\,\theta\,t\,T_m} e_1 \big){(1-\theta)}^m\,\mathrm{d}\theta . $$
nodes.section: 2 Problem setting, Krylov approximation, and defect-based representation of the approximation error
nodes.statement_short: Integral form of the Taylor remainder $R_{m+1}(t)$ showing its dependence on $m$.

nodes.name: Defect-integral error bound
nodes.statement: For the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} we have $\| E(t-s) \|_2 \leq 1$ for $0\leq s \leq t$, and~\eqref{LDint} implies \begin{equation*} \|L_m(t)v\|_2 = \Big\| \int_0^t E(t-s)\,D_m(s)v\,\mathrm{d} s\ \Big\|_2 \leq \int_0^t \|D_m(s)v\|_2\,\mathrm{d} s. \end{equation*} With $\|v_{m+1}\|_2 = 1$, and \begin{subequations} \begin{equation} \delta_m(s) = e_m^\ast\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,s\,T_m}e_1 = \big( {\rm e}^{\sigma\,s\,T_m} \big)_{m,1}, \end{equation} together with~\eqref{Dm(s)v} we obtain \begin{equation} \|L_m(t)v\|_2 \leq \tau_{m+1,m} \int_0^t |\delta_m(s)| \, \mathrm{d} s. \end{equation} \end{subequations}
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.statement_short: In the nonexpansive case the error norm is bounded by $\tau_{m+1,m}\int_0^t|\delta_m(s)|ds$.

nodes.name: Matrix functions via Hermite interpolation on the spectrum
nodes.statement: To approximate the error integral in~\eqref{errorapprox1} we use the representation of matrix exponentials via Hermite interpolation of the scalar exponential function on the spectrum of the matrix~$ T_m $, see~\cite[Chap.~1]{higham08}: If $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_r$ ($ r \leq m $) denote the distinct eigenvalues of~$ T_m $ and $ n_j $ is the dimension of the largest Jordan block associated with~$ \mu_j $, then \begin{equation} {\rm e}^{\sigma\,t T_m} = p_t(T_m), \end{equation} where $ p_t(\lambda) $ is the {Hermite} interpolant of degree $ \leq m-1 $ of the function \begin{equation} {f_t}(\lambda) = {\rm e}^{\sigma\,t\lambda} \end{equation} over the nodes $ \mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m $ in the sense of~\cite[(1.7)]{higham08}, \begin{equation*} p_t^{(\ell)}(\mu_j) = f_t^{(\ell)}(\mu_j), \quad j=1,\ldots,r, \quad \ell=0,\ldots,n_j-1. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
assumptions: $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_r$ ($ r \leq m $) denote the distinct eigenvalues of~$ T_m $
$ n_j $ is the dimension of the largest Jordan block associated with~$ \mu_j $
nodes.statement_short: $e^{\sigma tT_m}=p_t(T_m)$ with $p_t$ the Hermite interpolant of $e^{\sigma t\lambda}$ on the spectrum of $T_m$.

nodes.name: $T_m$ is nonderogatory
nodes.statement: \wa{For a general matrix, the degree of $ p_t $ may be smaller than $ m-1 $. However, in our context a special case occurs: Since the lower diagonal entries of $ T_m $ do not vanish, $ T_m $ is nonderogatory, i.e., for each eigenvalue $ \mu_j $ the associated eigenspace is one-dimensional, see~\cite[Section~3.1]{horn85}. Then, $ \sum_{j=1}^{r} n_j = m $, which implies that the degree of $ p_t $ is exactly $ m-1 $.
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
assumptions: the lower diagonal entries of $ T_m $ do not vanish
conclusions: the degree of $ p_t $ is exactly $ m-1 $

nodes.name: Eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m$ of $T_m$
nodes.statement: \wa{In the following we denote the full sequence of the $ m $ eigenvalues of $ T_m $ by $ \lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m $.
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}

nodes.name: Divided-difference representation of $\delta_m$
nodes.statement: \noindent Let $T_m \in \mathbb C^{m\times m}$ be an upper Hessenberg matrix with eigenvalues $ \lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m $ and $ \text{spec}(\sigma T_m) \subseteq \mathbb C_- $. Then the function $ \delta_m(t) $ defined as in~\eqref{defdelta}, i.e., \begin{equation*} \delta_m(t) = e_m^\ast\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,t\,T_m}e_1 = \big( {\rm e}^{\sigma\,t\,T_m} \big)_{m,1}, \end{equation*} satisfies \begin{equation} \delta_m(t) = \divdif{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m}{f_t} \gamma_m \leq {\frac{t^{m-1}}{(m-1)!}\,\gamma_m,} \end{equation} with $ \gamma_m $ from~\eqref{gammam} and where $\divdif{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m}{f_t}$ is the {$ (m-1) $-th} divided difference over $ \text{\rm spec}(T_m) $ of the function $ f_t $ defined in~\eqref{def:thetadd}.
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
assumptions: Let $T_m \in \mathbb C^{m\times m}$ be an upper Hessenberg matrix with eigenvalues $ \lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m $
nodes.statement_short: $\delta_m(t)$ equals $\gamma_m$ times the $(m-1)$-th divided difference of $e^{\sigma t\lambda}$ on spec$(T_m)$, hence $\le t^{m-1}\gamma_m/(m-1)!$.
nodes.label: prop:prop1

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (divided differences)
nodes.statement: We proceed from the Newton representation of the interpolant $p_t(\lambda) $ from~\eqref{pt}, \begin{equation*} p_t(\lambda) = \sum_{j=0}^{m-1} \divdif{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{j+1}}{f_t}\,\omega_j(\lambda), \end{equation*} with $ \omega_j(\lambda) = (\lambda-\lambda_1) \cdots (\lambda-\lambda_{j}) $. {From~\eqref{eTe} and by definition of $ \gamma_m $, it is obvious that the $ \omega_j $ satisfy} \begin{equation*} e_m^\ast\,\omega_j(T_m)\,e_1 = \left\{\begin{array}{ll} 0, & j=0,\ldots,m-2, \\ \gamma_m,& j=m-1. \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} Together with~\eqref{pt} this shows that the identity claimed in~\eqref{deltam-repr} is valid: \begin{equation*} \delta_m(t) = e_m^\ast\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,t T_m}\,e_1 = e_m^\ast\,p_t(T_m) e_1 = \sum_{j=0}^{m-1} \divdif{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{j+1}}{f_t} e_m^\ast\,\omega_j(T_m)e_1 = \divdif{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m}{f_t} \gamma_m. \end{equation*} According to~\cite[(B.28)]{higham08} the divided difference can be estimated by \begin{align*} &|f_t[\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m]| \leq \frac{\max_{z \in \Omega} D^{(m-1)}f_t(z)}{(m-1)!}\\ &\text{for convex $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb C$ which contains all eigenvalues $ \lambda_j$.} \end{align*} With $D^{(m-1)}f_t(\lambda) = (\sigma\,t)^{m-1} {\rm e}^{\sigma\,t\lambda} $, $ |\sigma|=1 $ and $\text{Re}(\sigma \lambda_j)\leq 0$ we obtain \begin{equation*} |\divdif{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m}{f_t}| \leq \frac{t^{m-1}}{(m-1)!}, \end{equation*} which implies the estimate~\eqref{deltam-repr} for $ \delta_m(t) $. \qed
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.statement_short: Newton form of the Hermite interpolant: only the last Newton term survives in the $(m,1)$ entry; bound the divided difference by the derivative.

nodes.name: Computable upper bound
nodes.statement: \noindent For the nonexpansive case the error $ L_m(t)v $ of the Krylov approximation~\eqref{Smv} to $ E(t)v $ satisfies \begin{equation} \| L_m(t)v \|_2 \leq \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m\,\frac{t^{m}}{m!} \end{equation} with $ \tau_{m+1,m} $ from~\eqref{krylovidentity} and $ \gamma_m $ from~\eqref{gammam}.
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.statement_short: In the nonexpansive case $\|L_m(t)v\|_2\le \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m t^m/m!$ ($\mathrm{Err}_a$).
nodes.label: theorem:upperboundexp

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (computable upper bound)
nodes.statement: We proceed from~\eqref{errestintdefect}. For $ \delta_m $ defined in~\eqref{defdelta}, Proposition~\ref{prop:prop1} implies \begin{equation*} |\delta_m(s)| \leq \frac{s^{m-1}}{(m-1)!} \gamma_m, \end{equation*} and this gives an upper bound for the error integral~\eqref{errorapprox1}: \begin{equation*} \|L_m(t)v\|_2 \leq \tau_{m+1,m} \gamma_m \int_0^t \frac{s^{m-1}}{(m-1)!}\,\mathrm{d} s = \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m \frac{t^{m}}{m!}, \end{equation*} which completes the proof. \tjnew{ Proposition~\ref{prop:prop1} is applied here in the nonexpansive case ($ W(\sigma A) \subseteq \mathbb C_- $) which implies the requirement $ \text{spec}(\sigma T_m) \subseteq \mathbb C_- $, see~\eqref{subsetofspectrum}.} \qed
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.statement_short: Insert the divided-difference bound on $|\delta_m(s)|$ into the defect integral and integrate.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{Err}_a$ matches the leading error term
nodes.statement: The upper bound~\eqref{asyerrest} corresponds to the 2-norm of the leading error term~\eqref{asy-leading} according to Proposition~\ref{prop:prop3}. It is easily computable from the \tjnew{Krylov} decomposition~\eqref{krylovidentity}.
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}

nodes.name: Error estimate $\mathrm{Err}_a$
nodes.statement: We denote the error estimate given by~\eqref{asyerrest} as \begin{equation}\tag{$\mathrm{Err}_a$} \mathrm{Err}_a = \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m\,\frac{t^{m}}{m!}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}

nodes.name: Asymptotical correctness
nodes.statement: \noindent The upper bound~\eqref{asyerrest} is asymptotically correct for $ t \to 0 $, i.e., \begin{equation} \| L_m(t)v \|_2 = \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m\,\frac{t^m}{m!} + {\mathcal{O}}(t^{m+1}). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
conclusions: The upper bound~\eqref{asyerrest} is asymptotically correct
nodes.statement_short: $\|L_m(t)v\|_2 = \mathrm{Err}_a + O(t^{m+1})$.
nodes.label: prop:prop4

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (asymptotical correctness)
nodes.statement: The asymptotic estimate \begin{align*} \bigg| \| L_m(t)v \|_2 - \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m\,\frac{t^m}{m!} \bigg| &= \bigg| \| L_m(t)v \|_2 - \Big\| \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m\,\frac{(\sigma\,t)^{m}}{m!}v_{m+1} \Big\|_2 \bigg| \\ &\leq \Big\| L_m(t)v - \tau_{m+1,m}\gamma_m\,\frac{(\sigma\,t)^{m}}{m!}v_{m+1} \Big\|_2 = {\mathcal{O}}(t^{m+1}) \end{align*} is valid due to~Proposition~\ref{prop:prop3}, and this proves~\eqref{asyerrcorr}. \qed
nodes.section: 3 An upper error bound \tjnew{for the \tjnew{nonexpansive case} in~2.1}
nodes.statement_short: Reverse triangle inequality against the leading error term of Proposition (leading term).

nodes.name: Shift-and-invert Krylov approximations
nodes.statement: In \cite[Section 4]{eshhoc06} a defect-based error formulation is given for the shift-and-invert Krylov approximation of the matrix exponential function. In contrast to the standard Krylov method, the defect is not of order $m-1$ for $t\to 0$ there. Hence, our new results do not directly apply to shift-and-invert Krylov approximations. A study of a posteriori error estimates for the shift-and-invert approach is a topic of future investigations.

nodes.name: $\varphi$-functions
nodes.statement: As another application we consider the so-called $ \varphi $-functions, with power series representation \begin{subequations} \begin{equation} \varphi_p(z) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{z^k}{(k+p)!}, \quad p\geq 0. \end{equation} We have $ \varphi_0(z) = {\rm e}^z $, and \begin{equation} \varphi_p(z) = \frac{1}{(p-1)!} \int_0^1 (1-\theta)^{p-1}{\rm e}^{\theta z}\,\mathrm{d}\theta, \quad p \geq 1. \end{equation} \end{subequations}
nodes.section: 4 Krylov approximation to $\varphi$-functions.

nodes.name: Krylov approximation of $\varphi$-functions
nodes.statement: Krylov approximation is a common technique to evaluate $\varphi$-functions of matrices applied to a starting vector, \begin{equation} \varphi_p(\sigma\,t A)v \approx V_m \varphi_p(\sigma\,t T_m) e_1,~~~~p\geq 0. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4 Krylov approximation to $\varphi$-functions.

nodes.name: Error $L^p_m(t)v$ for $\varphi$-functions
nodes.statement: We use the following notation for the error in the $\varphi$-functions: \begin{equation} L^p_m(t)v = \varphi_p(\sigma\,t\,A)v - V_m \varphi_p(\sigma\,t\,T_m) e_1. \end{equation} With~\eqref{generalizeerrornotation} we generalize the previously used notation: $ L_m(t) = L^0_m(t) $.
nodes.section: 4 Krylov approximation to $\varphi$-functions.

nodes.name: Upper bound for Krylov approximation of $\varphi$-functions
nodes.statement: The error of the Krylov approximation~\eqref{kry-phi} to $ \varphi_p(\sigma\,t A)v $ with $ p \geq 0 $ satisfies \begin{subequations} \begin{equation} L^p_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m}\,\gamma_m \frac{(\sigma\, t)^m}{(m+p)!} \, v_{m+1} + \mathcal{O}(t^{m+1}). \end{equation} Furthermore, \tjnew{in the nonexpansive case} its norm is bounded by \begin{equation} \|L^p_m(t)v \|_2 \leq \tau_{m+1,m}\,\gamma_m\,\frac{t^{m}}{(m+p)!}, \end{equation} \end{subequations} and this bound is asymptotically correct for $ t \to 0 $.
nodes.section: 4 Krylov approximation to $\varphi$-functions.
conclusions: this bound is asymptotically correct for $ t \to 0 $
nodes.statement_short: The $\varphi_p$ Krylov error has leading term $\tau\gamma_m(\sigma t)^m/(m+p)!\,v_{m+1}$ and is bounded by $\tau\gamma_m t^m/(m+p)!$.
nodes.label: theorem:upperboundphi

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem ($\varphi$-functions)
nodes.statement: For $p=0$ the result directly follows from Propositions~\ref{prop:prop3},~\ref{prop:prop4} and Theorem~\ref{theorem:upperboundexp}. We now assume $ p \geq 1 $. Via the series representation~\eqref{defphiseries} of $\varphi_p$ we can determine the leading term of the error in an analogous way as in Proposition~\ref{prop:prop3}: \begin{align*} \varphi_p(\sigma\,t A)v - V_m \varphi_p(\sigma\,t T_m) e_1 &= \frac{(\sigma\,t)^m \,(A^m v - V_m T_m^m e_1)}{(m+p)!} + \mathcal{O}(t^{m+1}) \\ &= \tau_{m+1,m}\,\gamma_m \frac{(\sigma\, t)^m}{(m+p)!} \, v_{m+1} + \mathcal{O}(t^{m+1}), \end{align*} which proves~\eqref{leadingtermphij}. Furthermore, proceeding from~\eqref{defphiint} we obtain \begin{align*} \varphi_p(\sigma\,t A)v - V_m \varphi_p(\sigma\,t T_m) e_1 &= \frac{1}{(p-1)!} \int_0^1 (1-\theta)^{p-1}\big( {\rm e}^{\sigma\,\theta\,t A} v - V_m\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,\theta\,t T_m} e_1 \big) \,\mathrm{d} \theta\\ &= \frac{1}{(p-1)!} \int_0^1 (1-\theta)^{p-1} L_m(\theta\,t)v \,\mathrm{d} \theta, \end{align*} with the error $L_m(t)v$ for the matrix exponential case. Now we apply Theorem~\ref{theorem:upperboundexp} to obtain \begin{align*} \| \varphi_p(\sigma\,t A)v - V_m \varphi_p(\sigma\,t T_m) e_1 \|_2 &\leq \frac{1}{(p-1)!} \int_0^1 (1-\theta)^{p-1} \|L_m(\theta\,t)v\|_2 \,\mathrm{d} \theta\\ &\leq \tau_{m+1,m}\,\gamma_m\,\frac{t^m}{(p-1)!\,m!} \int_0^1 (1-\theta)^{p-1} \theta^m \,\mathrm{d} \theta\\ &= \tau_{m+1,m}\,\gamma_m\,\frac{t^{m}}{(m+p)!}, \end{align*} which proves~\eqref{eresphij}. \qed
nodes.section: 4 Krylov approximation to $\varphi$-functions.
nodes.statement_short: Series representation for the leading term; integral representation of $\varphi_p$ reduces the bound to the exponential case.

nodes.name: Saad's error representation
nodes.statement: {{\rm{see~\cite[Theorem 5.1]{saad92s}}}} With the $\varphi$-functions defined in~\eqref{defphi}, the error~\eqref{Lerror} can be represented in the form \begin{align} L_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m}\,\sigma\,t \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} e_m^\ast\varphi_{j}(\sigma\,tT_m)\,e_1 (\sigma\,t A)^{j-1}v_{m+1}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Error estimate $\mathrm{Err}_1$
nodes.statement: Analogously to~\cite[Section 5.2]{saad92s} we use the notation $\mathrm{Err}_1$ for the norm of this term, \begin{equation}\tag{$\mathrm{Err}_1$} \mathrm{Err}_1 = \tau_{m+1,m}\,t\,|e_m^\ast\varphi_1(\sigma\,t T_m)e_1|. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Augmented matrix formula for $\varphi_1$
nodes.statement: According to~\cite[Proposition~2.1]{saad92s}, $\varphi_1(\sigma\,t T_m)$ can be computed from the extended matrix \begin{subequations} \begin{equation} {T}^+_m = \begin{bmatrix} T_m&0\\ \tau_{m+1,m}\,e_m^\ast&0 \end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb C^{(m+1)\times (m+1)} \end{equation} as \begin{equation} {\rm e}^{\sigma\,t{T}^+_m} e_1= \begin{bmatrix} {\rm e}^{\sigma\,tT_m}e_1\\ \tau_{m+1,m}\,\sigma\,t \,(e_m^\ast\,\varphi_1(\sigma\,t T_m)\,e_1) \end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb C^{m+1}. \end{equation} \end{subequations}
nodes.section: 5 Corrected Krylov approximation for the exponential and $\varphi$-functions.
nodes.statement_short: $\varphi_1(\sigma tT_m)$ entries appear in the exponential of the extended matrix $T^+_m$.

nodes.name: Corrected Krylov approximation
nodes.statement: Equation~\eqref{computephi1} can be used to evaluate the error estimate $\mathrm{Err}_1$ or a corrected Krylov approximation in the form \begin{equation} {S}^+_m(t)v = {V}^+_m\,{\rm e}^{\sigma\,t{T}^+_m}e_1 \text{~~~with~~~} {V}^+_m=\Big[ V_m\,\big|\,v_{m+1} \Big] \in\mathbb C^{n\times (m+1)}, \end{equation} for which the first term of the error expansion according to Proposition~\ref{prop:saad92} vanishes, see~\cite{saad92s}.
nodes.section: 5 Corrected Krylov approximation for the exponential and $\varphi$-functions.

nodes.name: Error $L^+_m(t)v$ of the corrected approximation
nodes.statement: For the error of the corrected Krylov approximation we use the notation \begin{equation*} L_m^+(t)v = E(t)v - {S}^+_m(t)v. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Corrected Krylov approximation of $\varphi$-functions
nodes.statement: The corrected Krylov approximation to $\varphi_p(\sigma\,t\,A)v$ is given in~\cite[Theorem 2]{sidje98}: \begin{equation*} \varphi_p(\sigma\,t\,A)v \approx {V}^+_m \varphi_p(\sigma\,t\,{T}^+_m) e_1 \end{equation*} with ${T}^+_m$ and ${V}^+_m$ given in~\eqref{definetcor} and~\eqref{Smbar}.

nodes.name: Error $L^{p,+}_m(t)v$
nodes.statement: The error of the corrected Krylov approximation is denoted by \begin{equation} L^{p,+}_m(t)v = \varphi_p(\sigma\,t\,A)v - {V}^+_m \varphi_p(\sigma\,t\,{T}^+_m) e_1. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Error series for standard and corrected $\varphi$-function approximations
nodes.statement: \begin{subequations} The error of the Krylov approximation $L^p_m(t)v$, see~\eqref{generalizeerrornotation}, satisfies \begin{equation} L^p_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m} \sigma\,t \sum_{j=p+1}^{\infty} (e_m^\ast \varphi_j(\sigma\,t\,T_m) e_1) \,(\sigma\,t\,A)^{j-p-1} v_{m+1}. \end{equation} The error of the corrected Krylov approximation $L^{p,+}_m(t)v$, see~\eqref{generalizeerrornotation2}, is given by \begin{equation} L^{p,+}_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m} \sigma\,t \sum_{j=p+2}^{\infty} (e_m^\ast \varphi_j(\sigma\,t\,T_m) e_1) \,(\sigma\,t\,A)^{j-p-1} v_{m+1}. \end{equation} \end{subequations}

nodes.name: Asymptotic correctness of $\mathrm{Err}_1$ estimators
nodes.statement: From the representation~\eqref{defphiseries} for the $\varphi_j$ together with~\eqref{eTe} and~\eqref{gammam} we observe \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} e_m^\ast \varphi_j(\sigma t T_m) e_1 &= \frac{(\sigma t)^{m-1} e_m^\ast T_m^{m-1}\,e_1}{(m-1+j)!} + \mathcal{O}(t^m) = \gamma_m \,\frac{(\sigma t)^{m-1}}{(m-1+j)!} + \mathcal{O}(t^m). \end{aligned} \end{equation} By~\eqref{em-phi-e1} we observe $ e_m^\ast\varphi_{j}(\sigma\,tT_m)\,e_1 = \mathcal{O}(t^{m-1}) $ for $ j \geq 0 $ and we conclude that the asymptotically leading order term of $ L^p_m(t)v $ for $ t \to 0 $ is obtained by the leading term ($j=p+1$) of the series~\eqref{generalizeerrorSaadsum1}: \begin{subequations} \begin{equation} L^p_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m} \sigma\,t (e_m^\ast \varphi_{p+1}(\sigma\,t\,T_m) e_1 ) v_{m+1} + \mathcal{O}(t^m). \end{equation} Analogously we obtain the asymptotically leading order term of $ L^{p,+}_m(t)v $ for $ t \to 0 $ by the leading term ($j=p+2$) of the series~\eqref{generalizeerrorSaadsum2}: \begin{equation} L^{p,+}_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m} (\sigma\,t)^2 (e_m^\ast \varphi_{p+2}(\sigma\,t\,T_m) e_1) \,A v_{m+1} + \mathcal{O}(t^{m+1}). \end{equation} \end{subequations} The asymptotically leading terms in~\eqref{Lpleadingtermsum} and~\eqref{Lpplusleadingtermsum} can be used as error estimators: \begin{subequations} \begin{equation} \|L^p_m(t)v\|_2 \approx \tau_{m+1,m}\,t |e_m^\ast \varphi_{p+1}(\sigma\,t\,T_m) e_1| \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \|L^{p,+}_m(t)v\|_2 \approx \|A v_{m+1}\|_2 \tau_{m+1,m}\,t^2 |e_m^\ast \varphi_{p+2}(\sigma\,t\,T_m) e_1|. \end{equation} \end{subequations} The error estimators~\eqref{LPnextphierrorest} and~\eqref{LPplusnextphierrorest} are already suggested in \cite{sidje98,niewri12}. We will refer to them as $\mathrm{Err}_1$ in the context of the $\varphi$-functions with standard and corrected Krylov approximation, generalizing the corresponding quantities for the exponential case $p=0$.

nodes.name: Upper bound for corrected Krylov approximation
nodes.statement: The error of the corrected Krylov approximation~\eqref{generalizeerrornotation2} to $ \varphi_p(\sigma\,t A)v $ with $ p \geq 0 $ satisfies \begin{subequations} \begin{equation} L^{p,+}_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m}\,\gamma_m \frac{(\sigma\, t)^{m+1}}{(m+p+1)!} \, A v_{m+1} + \mathcal{O}(t^{m+2}). \end{equation} Furthermore, \tjnew{in the nonexpansive case} its norm is bounded by \begin{equation} \|L^{p,+}_m(t)v\|_2 \leq \|A v_{m+1}\|_2\, \tau_{m+1,m}\,\gamma_m \frac{t^{m+1}}{(m+p+1)!}, \end{equation} \end{subequations} and this bound is asymptotically correct for $ t \to 0 $.

conclusions: this bound is asymptotically correct for $ t \to 0 $

nodes.label: theorem:asymerrorpricorrected

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (corrected approximation)
nodes.statement: Applying~\eqref{em-phi-e1} (with $j=p+2$) to~\eqref{Lpplusleadingtermsum} shows~\eqref{leadingtermphijcor}: \begin{equation*} L^{p,+}_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m}\, \gamma_m\, \frac{(\sigma\,t)^{m+1}}{(m+p+1)!} \,A v_{m+1} + \mathcal{O}(t^{m+2}). \end{equation*} From Proposition~\ref{prop:generalSaadsum} we observe \begin{align*} L^{p,+}_m(t)v = \sigma\,t\,A \,\,L^{p+1}_m(t)v. \end{align*} Using the integral representation analogously as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{theorem:upperboundphi} for $L^{p+1}_m(t)v$ and formula~\eqref{LDint} for $L_m(t)v$, we obtain \begin{align*} L^{p,+}_m(t)v &= \sigma\,t\,A\,\, L^{p+1}_m(t)v = \tau_{m+1,m} \sigma\,t \frac{1}{p!} \int_0^1 (1-\theta)^{p} A\, L_m(\theta\,t)v \,\mathrm{d} \theta\\ &= \tau_{m+1,m} \sigma\,t \frac{1}{p!} \int_0^1 (1-\theta)^{p} \int_0^{\theta t} {\rm e}^{\sigma (\theta t-s) A} A v_{m+1} \delta_m( s)\,\mathrm{d} s \,\mathrm{d} \theta. \end{align*} With norm inequalities \tjnew{(note the nonexpansive case)} and Proposition~\ref{prop:prop1} we obtain \begin{align*} \|L^{p,+}_m(t)v\|_2 &\leq \tau_{m+1,m} \,t\,\|A v_{m+1}\|_2 \frac{1}{p!} \int_0^1 (1-\theta)^{p} \int_0^{\theta t} |\delta_m( s)|\,\mathrm{d} s \,\mathrm{d} \theta\\ &\leq \|A v_{m+1}\|_2 \tau_{m+1,m} \gamma_m\, t^{m+1}\,\frac{1}{p!\,m!} \int_0^1 (1-\theta)^{p} \theta ^m\,\mathrm{d} s \,\mathrm{d} \theta\\ &= \|A v_{m+1}\|_2 \tau_{m+1,m} \gamma_m \frac{t^{m+1}}{(m+p+1)!}, \end{align*} which proves~\eqref{eresphijcor}. \tjnew{Proposition~\ref{prop:prop1} is applied here in the nonexpansive case, see also the proof of Theorem \ref{theorem:upperboundexp}.}\hfill\qed
